title: Channel coding over BPSK and AWGN
description: Scenario 4: channel coding over BPSK and AWGN.

parameters.conv: K = 7, (133, 171), k = 1024 + 6 tail bits, soft Viterbi; Eb/N0 = 1, 2, 3, 4 dB
parameters.nr_ldpc: 5G NR LDPC, k = 1024, n = 2048 (base graph 2, Z = 104), flooding sum-product, 50 iterations; Eb/N0 = 1, 1.5, 2, 2.5 dB
parameters.ldpc_same_llr: PEG (1024, 512), flooding sum-product, 50 iterations, identical LLRs; Eb/N0 = 1.5, 2, 2.5, 3 dB
parameters.timing: 200 frames (quick: 20) at Eb/N0 = 3 dB (conv) or 2 dB (LDPC); OptiCommPy without numba: 2 frames

libraries.comnum: comnum from Python: the functions of the comnum package, called block by block
libraries.comnum-spec: comnum from Python: comnum.run_spec, the parallel Monte Carlo runner of Rust
libraries.opticommpy: OptiCommPy with numba (its @njit kernels compiled; its CuPy split-step on the GPU in the mode gpu)
libraries.sionna: Sionna PHY (PyTorch, eager mode; the CPU, or the GPU in the mode gpu)

nr_ldpc.comnum-spec: the specification format has no 5G NR LDPC code (NrLdpc: Python and Rust API)
nr_ldpc.opticommpy: no 5G NR LDPC code (its decoder takes a parity-check matrix: see ldpc_same_llr)

ldpc_same_llr.comnum-spec: the runner draws its own channel (this case feeds the same LLRs to every decoder)
